chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: Lester Young replaces Ben Webster; the era of well-trained musicians
summary: Lester Young joined Kirk after Webster left for Cab Calloway, before going to Basie. She compares Lester's freedom with Webster's economy, and says the era bred Parker and Dizzy.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Who were some of the other musicians who were around in Kansas City?
The great names like Lester, Jo Jones, Walter -(Page)
When did you first run into Lester Young?
When Ben Webster left (the) Andy Kirk to join Cab Calloway, Lester Young joined us in Kansas City, but he didn't stay with us very long because shortly after that he went to Count Basie's band.
When Lester followed someone like Ben Webster wasn't there a problem of the difference of sound?

Yes, we missed Ben Webster on account of sound but Lester was more free and whatnot in solos to play a hundred solos and never repeat. Ben Webster was the type of guy that could put so much in one bar. If you played with him he could do so much with one bar than any other man could do. Lester would play 12 or 15 choruses and each one of them would sound different. But with a man in the band like Ben, you'd miss him.
Was Lester appreciated in Kansas City?

Oh, yes. In other words, that was the era of the well-trained musician, that was the last of the well-trained musicians. Out of that era came Charlie Parker, Dizzy, and the bop era. These musicians, we never went out against each other, say, I'm going to outplay another pianist. We had some terrific women around. We'd just exchange ideas and play and have a ball and drink and eat together, but we never had that thing that someone's going to cut you completely out or make a fool out of you.
